entries.title: Nahum 3:1
segments:
vv 1-3. 
 
When a city is full of robbery and murder within, God will bring upon its inhabitants robbery and murder from without, and take away from them all power of resistance.

entries.title: Nahum 3:2
segments: The noise of a whip; a new description of the invading hosts, with the slaughter which they make in Nineveh.

entries.title: Nahum 3:4
segments:
Because of the multitude--through her witchcrafts; this verse assigns the reason of God's judgments upon Nineveh.  She is compared to a beautiful harlot, who is also a potent enchantress. Her lovers are her dependent kings and princes; her hire is the price which they pay her for the right of oppressing and plundering the nations she has conquered; and her enchantments are all the arts by which she attaches them to herself. 
 
vv 4-7. 
 
Rich and powerful nations have many and great means at their disposal, and are able to offer great inducements to the weaker nations that surround them to purchase their favor by becoming their allies in wickedness.  Their affairs are often managed with consummate policy, and for a long time they are very prosperous.  But if, as in the case of Nineveh, injustice and fraud lie at the foundation of their system, they must in the end be overthrown and put to shame before the whole world.  God's word, and the facts of history, combine to show that cunning management can never be a substitute for justice and truth in procuring for a nation permanent prosperity and strength.

entries.title: Nahum 3:8
segments:
Populous No; rather, "No-Amon," the celebrated metropolis of Upper Egypt, also called Thebes, lying on both sides of the Nile, whose waters served at once to enrich and defend it.  According to Homer it had a hundred gates, through each of which issued two hundred warriors in chariots.  In the time of Nahum it seems to have been recently destroyed, and he exhorts Nineveh to take warning from its fate. 
 
  The rivers; the Nile and its canals. 
 
  The sea; that is, the Nile, which the Arabs at the present day call "the sea."  See note on

. 
 
vv 8-10. 
 
The many instances on record of the sudden overthrow of rich and powerful cities, should be a warning to all cities and states that their prosperity depends upon God, who is able at any moment to take it away; and will take it away, if it be made the minister of pride, injustice, and "fleshly lusts which war against the soul."

entries.title: Nahum 3:9
segments:
Phut and Lubim; African nations: the latter are supposed to have been the Libyans. 
 
  Thy helpers; No-Amon is addressed.

entries.title: Nahum 3:11
segments:
Drunken; with the cup of God's wrath. 
 
  Shalt be hid; or, "shalt hide thyself."  Nineveh is addressed. 
 
  Seek strength; seek in vain a defence against the enemy. 
 
vv 11-15. 
 
It is easy for God, when he purposes to destroy a people for its sins, to take from it counsel and strength; thus making the nation that has long been a terror to the world, as defenceless as women, and giving it over an unresisting prey to its destroyers.

entries.title: Nahum 3:12
segments: First ripe figs; see note on

. 
 
  If they be shaken, they shall even fall; the fortresses of Nineveh shall fall into the hands of her enemies, as easily as early figs into the mouths of those who shake them.

entries.title: Nahum 3:15
segments:
There; that is, even in the midst of thy preparations for defence. 
 
  The canker-worm; the word in the original denotes a species of locust. 
 
  Make thyself many; that is, do this, yet shalt thou vanish, like swarms of locusts.

entries.title: Nahum 3:16
segments: Spoileth, and fleeth away; supply, So shall it be with thee. Compare

. 
 
vv 16-19. 
 
The pomp and riches and thronging multitudes of Nineveh have passed away utterly and for ever.  Only a few mounds of rubbish remain to tell where she once stood.  So shall all wicked cities and empires pass away that are built on injustice and oppression.  Men shall clap their hands at the report of their overthrow, and God's cause shall triumph from generation to generation.

entries.title: Nahum 3:17
segments: Thy crowned; or, thy princes.  It is the princes and captains of the Ninevites, with their vast array of followers, of which the prophet speaks.

entries.title: Nahum 3:18
segments:
Thy shepherds; his chiefs, who ought to have been watchful for the defence of Nineveh. 
 
  Slumber; give themselves up to indolent security. 
 
  Dwell; rather, "lie inactive."

entries.title: Nahum 3:19
segments: The bruit of thee; the report of thy destruction.  About the year before Christ 625, and almost a century after the date of this prophecy, Nineveh was taken by Nabopolassar of Babylon and Cyazares of Media.  After this the city continued to decline, until nothing remained but a mass of ruins to attest its ancient greatness.
